located_observations.observation: Connected adult hand and wrist grip the thick pale cream inked slab. A curved-band-and-oval navy relief image recurs on the exposed impression.
Two adult neighbours have visible faces and hands gripping a frontal printed sheet; the woman has an open speaking mouth and both look toward the work.
Date and time occupy the upper coral module, event/activity the blue module, and six factual rows the ivory module. All eleven copy entries can be read.
Stacked action photos and date-first right modules remain identifiable; photos are flush to outside edges and fill roughly56% of width.
Fresh imprint in upper photo and held sheet in lower photo are separated by a hard horizontal photo seam; no single central page cutout bridges that seam.

located_observations.observation: Korean counters and syllables are distinct with word spaces. Title and facts are heavier than the assigned medium/open-regular typographic roles.

residuals: Photo column fills about56% of canvas and has no requested outside margins; assigned action windows occupy about43% with margins.
English sits near the bottom of the lower held sheet, not on a substantial paper bridge between the views.
The printing slab's pale cream rough edge could read as wood or linoleum rather than recognizably rubber.
Title and support copy use heavy weights rather than the warmer medium title/open regular facts role.
